text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Ouyahia reveals new cabinet line-up with most members of outgoing executive reappointed to new team, in "compromise of high risks".
- Two dead and around 50 wounded in dual bomb attack on train near El Harrach suburb in Algiers.
- Government coalition, "an alliance of circumstance" which brings no real changes and with National Democratic Rally keeping all "sovereign" portfolios.

- Forty-six train passengers wounded in double bomb attack in El Harrach suburb of Algiers. Security forces kill 11 "terrorists" -- Moslem fundamentalist rebels -- on Tuesday in Saida province southwest of Algiers.

- Former provisional leader of outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), Abdelkader Hachani, to be tried on July 7 in Algiers. Hachani has been held in "preventive detention" for five years since he was alleged to have incited members of armed forces to rebel against officers. Trial follows his going on hunger strike on June 5.
- Prime Minister Ouyahia sets up government strongly dominated by National Democratic Rally.
- Prime minister seems to have had "all the difficulties in the world to form his cabinet since consultations...lasted nearly two weeks."
